subject: rstan 2.14 doesn't accept data.frames, causes compile error.

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: rstan 2.14 doesn't accept data.frames, causes compile error.
parts:
Perhaps this was an intentional change / correction - it caught me out because previously dataframes were acceptable.
 
R code to demonstrate:


library(rstan)
Y=data.frame(cbind(rnorm(20)),cbind(rnorm(20)))

sm='data{
  vector[2] Y[20];
}
parameters{
  real mu;
}
model{
  mu~normal(0,1);
for(i in 1:20){
  Y[i] ~ normal(mu,1);
}

}
'
stan(model_code=sm,data=list(Y=Y),iter=200)
stan(model_code=sm,data=list(Y=as.matrix(Y)),iter=200)

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan 2.14 doesn't accept data.frames, causes compile error.
parts:
On Wednesday, January 11, 2017 at 10:29:26 PM UTC-5, Bee wrote:
I think it seems natural to accept not only matrix/array but also data.frame/list of vector when a variable in Stan is like vector[K] some[N]. Could you tell me you have a plan to fix it?

If you have a data.frame, then it should allow you to find columns of that data.frame that are the same as the objects in the data block of the Stan program. What used to work but now doesn't is treating the data.frame as if it were a matrix, in which case all you have to do is as.matrix() it.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan 2.14 doesn't accept data.frames, causes compile error.
parts:
I'd rather fix the input format and have programs on the
outside conform to that. It's much much easier for us to maintain
and doc, and the interfaces are easier to understand.

I do understand that this goes against a lot of the R philosophy of trying
to guess what a client wants and then trying to munge data structures to
accomplish it with implicit conversions. Even simple things are problematic,
such as whether a size-one container and scalar are the same thing:

> a = c(5)

> b = 5

> a == b
[1] TRUE

Underlyingly, Stan is statically typed and treats integers and reals
as separate, and containers and scalars as spearate types.

- Bob
